widget.instructions: Press Play and pause at the top of the path.

stem: A ball is kicked at {{u}} m/s at {{ang}}° above the ground. Ignore air resistance.
What is its velocity at the highest point of its path?

options.text: Zero: it stops for an instant

args.text: If it stopped at the top, it would fall straight down from there. Play the flight and watch.

hints.text: Which part of the velocity changes during flight?
Gravity changes only the vertical velocity.
At the top, the vertical velocity is momentarily zero.

zero-velocity-at-top.text: Only the vertical part of the velocity is zero at the top. The horizontal part never changes.

vertical-velocity-at-top.text: At the top the ball stops rising, so it has no vertical velocity at all.

generic.text: At the top, only the horizontal velocity remains.

workedSolution.text: Horizontally there is no force, so vₓ = u cos θ = {{ux}} m/s throughout.
At the top v_y = 0, so the velocity is {{ux}} m/s horizontally.

zero-velocity-at-top.front: Velocity of a projectile at the top?
zero-velocity-at-top.back: Horizontal, equal to u cos θ. Only the vertical part is zero.

vertical-velocity-at-top.front: Direction of a projectile's velocity at the top?

generic.front: Velocity at the top of a projectile's path?

accessibility.altText: A ball's path as a projectile.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Choose an answer with the radio buttons; press Play to see the flight.
